name: Electronic Arts Inc.
quirks: DEAD TICKER: Electronic Arts was taken private in a ~$55B LBO by a consortium of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF, via Savvy Games Group), Silver Lake, and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners. The deal was announced 2025-09-29 at $210.00/share cash (a ~25% premium to the pre-announcement price of $168.32) and closed 2026-08-04. PIF ended up with ~93% ownership alongside Silver Lake and Affinity Partners. Financed with ~$36B equity and ~$20B new LBO debt (JPMorgan) -- reportedly the largest LBO in history.

EA delisted from NASDAQ: Form 25 filed by Nasdaq 2026-08-04, trading halted that day, shares suspended before the open 2026-08-05. EA filed Form 15 (deregistration) on 2026-08-14. Last 10-Q covers the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-03.

No current market price exists for EA. A DCF/dashboard valuation implying a live entry price was NOT built for this reason (same precedent as AVB/AvalonBay) -- it would misleadingly rank as a live opportunity in the screener. Yahoo's last quote (209.70, dated 2026-08-04) is a frozen tombstone print, not a tradeable price.

Financial history (SEC XBRL, FY2007-FY2026 annual + quarterlies, 104 periods) and qualitative analysis (EA_Analysis.json) were completed and are usable for historical/backward-looking research. Metrics CSV has no TotalDebt (XBRL tag not matched to EA's senior notes) -- left NULL, not assumed.

FY2026 (ended 2026-03-31) was EA's final full year as a public company: record $8.03B net bookings (+9% YoY), driven by Battlefield 6's October 2025 launch (20M+ copies, ~$1.4B revenue). Three rounds of layoffs occurred in 2026 including across all four Battlefield studios; new owners target ~$700M/year in cost cuts.
